introduction: Replace the --variant flag and the variant dimension from the tier table with an explicit --effort flag (and $AF_MODEL_EFFORT environment variable) so that reasoning effort is an independent setting that applies to any model — whether resolved from a tier or named by catalog id — with clamping checked before the run starts.

glossary.ModelChoice: The struct returned by ResolveModelNamed carrying the resolved *core.Model, the effective ThinkingLevel, and the spec string that produced them.
glossary.clamping: The process by which catalog.ClampThinkingLevel adjusts a requested thinking level to the nearest level the model supports, searching upward then downward (never downward to off).
glossary.effort: The reasoning effort level requested for a model run, one of the core.ThinkingLevel values: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max.
glossary.tier: A named capability level (SIMPLE, STANDARD, ADVANCED) that resolves to a vendor-specific catalog model and an optional thinking level via the tierTable.
glossary.tierTable: The map from (vendor, tier) to a catalog model spec and thinking level. After this spec, its type is map[string]map[ModelTier]tierEntry (the variant dimension is removed).

requirements.title: The --effort flag and $AF_MODEL_EFFORT
requirements.rationale: Reasoning effort must be an explicit, independent setting so an operator can override a tier's built-in effort or add effort to a model named by id.

criteria.action: register --effort as a string flag with accepted values off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the values of core.ThinkingLevelOrder), declared as an enum via DeclareEnum so --schema lists them
carry an Effort field of type string and no longer carry a Variant field

determine the run's effective effort by the first set source in this precedence: (1) --effort flag, (2) $AF_MODEL_EFFORT environment variable, (3) the tier's own effort when --model resolves to a tier name, (4) ThinkingUnset

criteria.condition: --effort is given with a model named by catalog id (not a tier)
criteria.action: apply the stated effort to that model, so effort works for model ids as well as tiers
match case-insensitively and store the value in its canonical lower-case form

criteria.condition: --effort is given a value outside the accepted set
criteria.action: exit with code 2 and list the accepted values in the error message
criteria.contract: exit code 2; stderr names the accepted values

criteria.condition: $AF_MODEL_EFFORT contains a value outside the accepted set
criteria.action: exit with code 2 and name the environment variable $AF_MODEL_EFFORT in the error message
criteria.contract: exit code 2; stderr names $AF_MODEL_EFFORT and the accepted values

requirements.title: Clamping is checked before the run
requirements.rationale: Without a pre-run clamp check, agentkit-go would silently drop an unsupported effort or the operator would discover the problem only after paying for a long run.

criteria.condition: the effective effort is set (not ThinkingUnset) after precedence resolution
criteria.action: call catalog.ClampThinkingLevel(model, effort) and use the clamped level as the run's effective effort

criteria.condition: the clamped level differs from the requested level
criteria.action: proceed at the clamped level and record a warning with code effort_clamped (a new WarnCode constant mapped to stage preflight in warnStages) whose message names both levels and the model

criteria.condition: ClampThinkingLevel returns ok==false and the effort was set explicitly (flag or env, steps 1 or 2 of the precedence)
criteria.action: fail before the first request with a usage error naming the model
criteria.contract: exit code 2; error message names the model that supports no reachable level

criteria.action: report the effective (clamped) level in model.thinking, not the requested one; the field's name, type and meaning are unchanged

requirements.title: --repair-model-effort on impl
requirements.rationale: The repair phase may need a different effort than the run's main model, especially when --repair-model names a different model whose tier has its own effort.

criteria.action: register --repair-model-effort with the same accepted values as --effort, in impl's Flags func, and add repair-model-effort to toolFlags["impl"] in toolflags.go

determine the repair phase's effective effort by the first set source: (1) --repair-model-effort, (2) if --repair-model is given: that model's own tier effort when it is a tier, otherwise ThinkingUnset (the run's --effort and $AF_MODEL_EFFORT do not carry over), (3) if --repair-model is not given: the run's effort
enable the repair phase (imply --repair) and run it on the run's model at the stated effort

criteria.condition: the repair phase's effort is clamped
criteria.action: record an effort_clamped warning whose message names the repair phase to distinguish it from the run's own clamping
provide no environment variable for --repair-model-effort, matching --repair-model which also has none

requirements.title: Remove the variant layer
requirements.rationale: The variant dimension existed for exactly one entry (anthropic ADVANCED extended). Removing it simplifies the tier table and eliminates a concept that only one vendor's table backed.

criteria.action: no longer register --variant, and remove the Variant field from the Common struct
change tierTable's type to map[string]map[ModelTier]tierEntry (removing the variant dimension) and delete the extended entry
change ModelSpec's signature to ModelSpec(name, vendor string) and ResolveModel's to ResolveModel(name, vendor string), removing the variant parameter
drop the variant argument from every call to ModelSpec and ResolveModel
add effort and remove variant from knownFixValueFlags
add variant to removedFlagMessages with a message directing the user to --effort and --model
display the removed-flag message directing the user to --effort and --model, rather than the generic 'flag provided but not defined' error
criteria.contract: exit code 2; stderr contains the removal message naming --effort and --model

requirements.title: Tier effort self-consistency
requirements.rationale: If a tier's prescribed effort is not accepted by its model, the tier table is at fault and the bug would only surface on a paid run. A test prevents that.

criteria.action: for any vendor and tier whose tierEntry has a non-unset thinking level, ClampThinkingLevel(model, level) shall return the same level (clamps to itself), verified by extending TestEveryTierOfEveryVendorResolvesInTheCatalog

requirements.title: Test coverage for removed and added behaviour
requirements.rationale: The variant tests must be deleted and replaced by effort tests; the schema golden files must reflect the flag changes.

criteria.action: delete TestTheExtendedVariantHasAMillionTokenWindow and TestAnUnknownVariantFallsBackToTheTierDefault from models_test.go

update the --schema golden files of all four tools (cmd/issue, cmd/fix, cmd/spec, cmd/impl) so they no longer contain variant and do contain effort; cmd/impl's golden also contains repair-model-effort

requirements.title: Documentation updates
requirements.rationale: Outdated docs are treated as regressions per the steering directives.

criteria.action: replace the --variant row in the shared-flags table with --effort, add --repair-model-effort to impl's flags, remove --variant from the --repair-model paragraph, and add an interface-versions entry recording the --variant removal and the --effort / --repair-model-effort addition

remove the extended paragraph and the --variant extended example from the tier section, add the effort precedence from 13-REQ-1.3, document $AF_MODEL_EFFORT, and add the long-context example --model anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 --effort xhigh
rewrite the repair paragraph to state 13-REQ-3.2's rule instead of referencing --vendor and --variant
add a closing note to §2 stating that the extended variant no longer exists and why
create docs/adr/08-effort-replaces-variant.md recording the decision: effort as an explicit setting independent of the model, and the removal of variants without compatibility

execution_paths.title: Operator overrides a tier's effort with --effort

steps.action: invokes a tool with --model ADVANCED --effort high
parses --effort high, normalises to lower-case, stores in Common.Effort
resolves ADVANCED to the tier's model (e.g. anthropic/claude-opus-5-5) and applies --effort high (step 1 of precedence) instead of the tier's xhigh
calls ClampThinkingLevel(model, high); if clamped, records effort_clamped warning
reports model.thinking as the effective (possibly clamped) level

execution_paths.title: Operator sets effort on a model named by catalog id

steps.action: invokes a tool with --model anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 --effort max
resolves the catalog id (no tier lookup), applies --effort max as the effective effort
calls ClampThinkingLevel(model, max); proceeds at the clamped level
reports model.thinking as the effective level

execution_paths.title: $AF_MODEL_EFFORT overrides a tier's effort when no flag is given

steps.action: sets AF_MODEL_EFFORT=low and invokes a tool with --model STANDARD (no --effort flag)
finds no --effort flag, reads $AF_MODEL_EFFORT=low (step 2 of precedence), overriding the tier's high
calls ClampThinkingLevel(model, low) and proceeds at the clamped level
reports model.thinking as the effective level

execution_paths.title: impl repair phase runs at its own effort

steps.action: invokes impl with --model STANDARD --effort low --repair-model ADVANCED --repair-model-effort high
resolves the run's model (STANDARD at low) and the repair model (ADVANCED at high, overriding the tier's xhigh)
runs the main phases at low effort on the STANDARD model
runs the repair phase at high effort on the ADVANCED model
reports each model's effective thinking level
invokes a tool with --variant extended
matches --variant in removedFlagMessages and exits with code 2, printing a message directing the user to --effort and --model
invokes a tool with --effort turbo
rejects the value, exits with code 2, and lists the accepted effort values in the error message
